doc: Log-log slope of the radially averaged power spectrum: (patch - mean) * Hann (np.hanning(n) outer itself, symmetric, 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi i / (n - 1))), np.fft.fft2 (unnormalized, complex128), fftshift, |F|^2, radius r = int(hypot(x, y)) with x, y counted from n // 2 (truncation), radial[r] = mean of the power at integer radius r (np.bincount), wavelength of bin k = n * patch_px_km() / k km; bins with lo <= wavelength <= hi (inclusive) and radial > 0 enter np.polyfit(log k, log radial, 1), whose slope is returned; fewer than 4 bins give NaN. n = patch.shape[0] (square patches only). A float32 patch: patch.mean() accumulates in float32 and the subtraction stays float32 (then times the float64 window). A port that accumulates the mean in float64 differs by 1.6e-6 relative on this smoothed patch (the float32 rounding of the data itself reaches the small high-wavenumber power): the golden float32 tolerance, 10x above it.
